decided_findings.scenario: Someone is chasing a screenshot failure and, to get the build past it for an hour, comments out the one line that tells the screenshot lane which files to photograph and drops in a different one. They mean to put it back. The build goes green — properly green, not skipped — so the reminder never arrives and the line stays commented for months. The lane still blocks merges, still runs, still reports success, and photographs nothing at all. The check written specifically to make that impossible looks at the file, finds the old line sitting there behind its two slashes, and counts it.
decided_findings.whats_wrong: Task 8 Step 2's last two assertions (lines 1655-1656) search the whole config text with no line anchor and no scoping to the `chromium` entry: `assert.match(config, /name:\s*'chromium'/, …)` and `assert.match(config, /testMatch:\s*'\*\*\/\*\.vr\.ts'/, …)`. Measured, both stay green over a config whose real `testMatch` line is commented out and replaced, over one whose `name: 'chromium'` line is commented out and renamed, and over one where the two projects' patterns have been swapped — leaving an unscoped CI run at exit 0 over zero pixels, the failure this task's opening paragraph describes. Every other assertion in the same suite is anchored to a real line (`/^\s+run: …$/m` at line 1880, `/^\s+container: …$/m` at line 1892, `/^IMAGE=…$/gm` at line 687) and the plan states the reason at line 1877: the unanchored form survives a commented-out line.
decided_findings.proposed_fix: Slice the config down to the `chromium` project entry — split on an anchored `name: 'chromium',` line and stop at that entry's own closing `},`, the way Task 9's web-job test slices ci.yml — then assert inside the slice with an anchored `/^\s+testMatch: '\*\*\/\*\.vr\.ts',$/m`. Keep the message `the chromium project is gone — the shots never run` on the `assert.ok` that tests the slice, so Task 8 Step 4 arm 3's quoted expectation still holds. Add a comment naming the three disguises the anchoring closes, since that is the reasoning the plan already writes down for its other anchored assertions.
decided_findings.why_it_works: All four states were run, not argued. The anchored, scoped pair is green on the healthy config and red on each of the three disguises the current pair sleeps through — a commented-out and replaced `testMatch`, a commented-out and renamed project, and the two projects' patterns swapped. The scoping is what catches the swap specifically: the `e2e` entry sits above the slice, so a `'**/*.vr.ts'` that lands on it is simply not in the text being searched. The anchoring is what catches the commented-out lines, which is the exact argument the plan already makes at line 1877 for the run-line assertion. And the repo's own Prettier leaves this config byte-identical, so the anchors are not fighting the formatter.

decided_findings.contradicts: The fix's two halves collide with EACH OTHER, which is the correction the spike found. (a) The filed unanchored regex PASSES against the helper as written - so it is green today, as intended. (b) It correctly FAILS when the flags are stripped from the real command - so on today's comment it does bite. (c) But with the flags stripped AND the helper's `--ignore-scripts` comment extended the way the finding's own second half asks, it PASSES - green over a broken helper. decided_findings.scenario: The script that runs the screenshot tests hands your whole working folder to a container and lets it write back. One flag on its install line is what stops every package you depend on from running its own setup code as the container's root user while that folder is attached. The identical line inside the build machine's copy is watched by a check that fails if the flag ever disappears. The local copy - the one running on your own machine, with your own files attached - is watched by nothing. Someone tidies the line, everything still passes, and the next install runs whatever those packages felt like running.
decided_findings.whats_wrong: Task 3 Step 3's guard reads only the `IMAGE=` line out of tooling/docker-playwright.sh, so the helper's `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` is unguarded - while Task 9 Step 7 anchors the byte-identical line in the `web` job and states the reason in a comment about dependency lifecycle scripts executing in CI. The asymmetry is not a decision anywhere in the plan; it is a gap in the file the plan is creating. The helper's own comment gives only the lefthook reason ('--ignore-scripts skips the lefthook `prepare`'), never the lifecycle-script one, so a later reader has nothing telling them the flag is load-bearing for anything else.
decided_findings.proposed_fix: Add one assertion to Task 3 Step 3's guard requiring the helper's install line, and anchor it past the flags - `/pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts && pnpm --filter/` - not the bare flag string the finding proposes. Extend the helper's `--ignore-scripts` comment to give the lifecycle-script reason alongside the lefthook one. The anchor is what lets both halves land together: with the bare form, the new comment would satisfy the new assertion and the guard would go green over a helper whose real command had lost the flags.
decided_findings.why_it_works: Measured on the helper text the plan actually writes. The bare form passes today and fails on a flags-stripped helper - but passes again once the comment carries the lifecycle wording the finding's own second half asks for, which is the defect reproduced end to end. The anchored form passes on the real helper and fails on both regressions, because `&& pnpm --filter` is command syntax no explanatory comment would carry. It also puts the control in the same file and the same test the plan is already creating, so nothing new is introduced - and it follows the idiom the plan states three times for exactly this hazard, most sharply where Task 9's guard has to be anchored because the job's own comment would otherwise fail it.

decided_findings.spike: RAN on real Playwright 1.61.1, and the premise HELD with one honest correction. Built a throwaway config in Task 1's two-project shape, gave the `chromium` project `timeout: 3_000`, and wrote a shot whose inner ceiling is HIGHER than the cap — `await expect(page.locator('#never-arrives')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10_000 })` on an element that never appears. Result: the test died at **3.0 s** with the headline `Test timeout of 3000ms exceeded.` — the project cap pre-empted the ceiling, exactly as filed, and exactly as the plan's own helper comment claims ('a per-test cap swallows a higher `expect` ceiling whole'). THE CORRECTION: the report is not as blind as the finding says. Underneath that headline Playwright still printed `Error: expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed`, `Locator: locator('#never-arrives')`, and the call log line `- Expect "toBeVisible" with timeout 10000ms`. So the pending signal IS named, and the filed harm — 'reports `Test timeout of 120000ms exceeded` instead of naming which readiness signal never arrived' — overstates it. The real cost is what survives that correction: the named ceilings never get to be the thing that fails, the diagnostic headline points at the cap rather than at the app, and `retries: 2` spends that whole budget three times.
decided_findings.scenario: The build machine is having a slow morning — the sound files take longer to fetch, the engine takes longer to wake up. Nothing is broken. Two of the nine screenshots give up anyway, because each one is allowed two minutes total while the individual waits inside them add up to nearly three. What you see is a message about the two-minute limit running out, and the run tries each of them twice more before going red. The plan wrote those individual waits precisely so that a failure would point at whichever part of the player never woke up. The overall limit fires first, so the number it points at is the limit.
decided_findings.whats_wrong: Task 1 Step 1 gives the `chromium` project `timeout: 120_000` (line 237) and justifies it with readiness alone (line 232): 'Readiness alone can spend 100 s (30 + 60 + 10) before a pixel is compared'. decided_findings.title: Playwright container pinned by mutable tag, and the new guard rejects a digest pin
decided_findings.section: Task 3: One shared container invocation, and a guard on its image tag
decided_findings.contradicts: The fix is right in direction but names too few sites, and the `after` corrects that. (1) THE THREE ENFORCED PINS MUST MOVE TOGETHER - the finding says this and it is right: Task 3's guard loops `for (const pin of pins) assert.equal(pin.trim(), ...)` over EVERY `container:` line in the workflow, so digest-pinning only the new `web` job while leaving the pre-existing `vr` job on the bare tag fails the guard outright. (2) TWO DOCUMENTATION SITES GO STALE AND NEITHER IS SCHEDULED: client/README.md:163 spells the bare tag inside its VR bullet, and docs/runbooks/vr-a11y-testing.md:37 says 'The `vr` CI job pins `container: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble`'. Task 10 Step 1 edits client/README.md only for two artifact names, and Task 10 Step 3 item 4 replaces the runbook's expanded docker block, not line 37. (3) FOUR MORE IN-PLAN SITES restate the bare tag and must be restated: Tech Stack (line 24), Global Constraints' Image tag bullet (line 33), Task 3 Step 4's prove-it step (which changes IMAGE to '...:v1.60.0-noble' and expects the message 'must pin mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble'), and Task 10 Step 1's rewrite of the NH-197 spec's Playwright-bump list. (4) FOOTPRINT: the `vr` job's container line is pre-existing ci.yml text this plan does not otherwise touch, and this plan tracks its own footprint carefully ('Two files sit outside the spec's stated footprint, and the PR body must declare both') - so the human should decide whether the digest lands here or as its own ticket.
decided_findings.spike: RAN, four ways, and it BOTH held and corrected the fix. (a) PREMISE MEASURED: I ran the plan's three guard assertions, transcribed verbatim, against a digest-suffixed pin. All three reject it - Task 3's helper arm and its ci.yml arm each fail `assert.equal`, and Task 9's `/^\s+container: mcr\.microsoft\.com\/playwright:v[\d.]+-noble$/m` does not match at all. Against the bare tag all three pass. So 'the plan locks the weaker form in' is measured fact, in exactly the three places named. (b) THE PROPOSED REGEXES WORK: both accept the digest form and reject the bare tag. (c) CORRECTION ONE - THE PROPOSED REGEXES ARE SHAPE-ONLY, WHICH RE-OPENS THE HOLE THEY WIDEN. I gave the helper digest A and the two container lines digests B and A; every proposed pattern still matched, so three homes can carry three DIFFERENT digests and the guard stays green - which is precisely the partial-bump failure the existing `assert.equal` exists to prevent. Capturing each digest and asserting exactly one distinct value across all three returns 2 distinct and fails, as it should. The fix must include that equality, not only the shape. (d) CORRECTION TWO - THE OBVIOUS WAY TO TAKE THE DIGEST PRODUCES A PIN THAT DOES NOT RESOLVE. `docker manifest inspect --verbose mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble` reports `sha256:cf0daee9b994042e011bc29f20cdff1a9f682a039b43fcd738f7d8a9d3bcd9d6`, and `docker manifest inspect <tag>@sha256:cf0daee9...` does NOT resolve. The registry serves a different digest per Accept header (a third, `sha256:b5812704...`, for its legacy default). The value that DOES resolve is `sha256:5b8f294aff9041b7191c34a4bab3ac270157a28774d4b0660e9743297b697e48`, confirmed by pulling the manifest by that digest, and the command that yields it is `docker buildx imagetools inspect <tag> --format '{{.Manifest.Digest}}'`. So the plan must name the command, or the next bump writes a pin that cannot be pulled. (e) UNTESTED: that GitHub Actions accepts a digest-suffixed `container:` value - I cannot run a workflow here. It is a standard Docker image reference and the runner passes it to `docker create`, but treat it as reasoned, and the human should confirm it on the first real run.
decided_findings.scenario: Every run of this gate - yours, and the one that decides whether a pull request can merge - downloads a container by a name that can be reassigned. Whoever can publish under that name can, tomorrow, put different code behind the same name, and it will run with your repository checked out and with your entire working folder attached read-write, including the folder of approved screenshots that the next commit sweeps up wholesale. Everywhere else this repository already refuses that: third-party build steps are pinned to exact unchangeable revisions, and package installs are held back for a week and blocked from downgrading. This one path is the exception. And the plan makes it permanent, because the three checks it adds compare the name letter for letter and would fail the moment someone tried to pin it properly.
decided_findings.whats_wrong: The container is pinned by a mutable tag in all three homes the plan creates or touches, and the plan's own guards make the immutable form fail. tooling/docker-playwright.sh's `IMAGE=mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble`, and the `container:` lines of the `vr` and `web` jobs, all name a tag that can be re-pushed; the helper attaches the developer's whole working tree with `-v "$PWD":/work`, and Tasks 4-7 each commit the snapshot folder with a directory-wide `git add`. Measured: a digest-suffixed pin fails Task 3 Step 3's `assert.equal` on the helper, fails the same assertion on the workflow pins, and fails Task 9 Step 7's `-noble$` anchor - three red assertions for a hardening change. Meanwhile pnpm-workspace.yaml sets `minimumReleaseAge: 10080` and `trustPolicy: no-downgrade`, and every third-party action in ci.yml is pinned to a 40-character commit SHA.
decided_findings.after:
Pin by digest in all three homes, and widen the guards so a digest is REQUIRED and all three must agree on it - the shape check alone is not enough (measured).

Task 3, Step 1:
```bash
# Re-take the digest on every Playwright bump, with buildx - NOT `docker manifest inspect --verbose`,
# whose reported digest does not resolve when used as a pin (measured against this registry, which
# serves a different digest per Accept header):
#   docker buildx imagetools inspect mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble --format '{{.Manifest.Digest}}'
IMAGE=mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble@sha256:5b8f294aff9041b7191c34a4bab3ac270157a28774d4b0660e9743297b697e48
```

Task 3, Step 3 - the guard, digest required AND identical across all three homes:
```js
  const withDigest = (prefix) =>
    new RegExp(`^${prefix}mcr\\.microsoft\\.com/playwright:v${floor}-noble@(sha256:[0-9a-f]{64})$`, 'gm');
  const grab = (text, prefix) => [...text.matchAll(withDigest(prefix))].map((m) => m[1]);
  const digests = [...grab(helper, 'IMAGE='), ...grab(workflow('ci.yml'), '\\s+container: ')];
  assert.equal(digests.length, 3, 'all three Playwright pins must carry a @sha256: digest');
  // Shape is not enough: three homes on three DIFFERENT digests all match the pattern, which is the
  // partial-bump hole this test exists to close. Require ONE value.
  assert.equal(new Set(digests).size, 1, `the three Playwright pins disagree: ${[...new Set(digests)].join(' vs ')}`);
```

Task 9, Step 1 and Step 7:
```yaml
  container: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble@sha256:5b8f294aff9041b7191c34a4bab3ac270157a28774d4b0660e9743297b697e48
```
```js
  assert.match(webJob, /^\s+container: mcr\.microsoft\.com\/playwright:v[\d.]+-noble@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$/m);
```

Plus the sites the finding does not name, all of which restate the bare tag: Global Constraints' Image tag bullet and the Tech Stack line; Task 3 Step 4's prove-it step and its expected message; Task 10 Step 1's NH-197 rewrite; and two documentation sites nothing currently schedules - client/README.md's VR bullet and docs/runbooks/vr-a11y-testing.md's 'The `vr` CI job pins ...' sentence.
decided_findings.proposed_fix: Pin the image by digest in all three enforced homes together - tooling/docker-playwright.sh's IMAGE= line and the container: lines of both the vr and web jobs - using the digest that actually resolves, taken with `docker buildx imagetools inspect <tag> --format '{{.Manifest.Digest}}'`. Widen both guards so the digest is required rather than rejected, AND capture the three digests and assert exactly one distinct value, because a shape-only pattern lets the three homes disagree. Add a Global Constraints line saying a Playwright bump re-takes the digest alongside the tag, naming the buildx command. Then restate the bare tag wherever else it is written: Global Constraints, Tech Stack, Task 3 Step 4's prove-it message, Task 10 Step 1's NH-197 rewrite, client/README.md's VR bullet and the runbook's vr-job sentence.
decided_findings.why_it_works: Measured end to end rather than reasoned. The three guards provably reject a digest today and provably accept it under the widened patterns, so the claim that the plan locks the weaker form in is fact, not inference. The digest-equality assertion is not decoration: with three homes carrying three different digests every proposed shape-only pattern still matched, which would have re-opened the exact partial-bump hole the existing assert.equal closes - the corrected form returns two distinct values and fails. And the digest value itself was resolved by pulling the manifest: the value docker manifest inspect --verbose reports does NOT resolve as a pin, so naming the buildx command is what stops the next bump writing an unpullable reference.

decided_findings.contradicts: The FACTS check out but the FIX collides with three settled things, so the `after` is reframed from a tenth shot to a cross-reference. (1) THE SPEC ALREADY DEFERS THIS STATE, and the reviewer missed it. docs/specs/2026-09-21-web-visual-regression-gate.md:394 lists the drag-over state under 'Candidates deliberately **not** in v1, each recorded so the omission is a decision rather than an oversight', names `.nh-drop-zone[data-dragging]` plus `.nh-drop-overlay`, names `fileDrag` and its CDP driver, and states the reason: 'out of v1 for screenshot **timing**, not missing tooling: each state exists only mid-gesture, so a shot has to pause before `drop` or `mouse.up()` and hold the frame steady long enough for two consecutive samples.' The finding never addresses that reason, so its fix does not answer the objection already on record. (2) Global Constraints caps the lane at nine and sets the bar for a tenth; Task 4 Step 3's header comment repeats it ('Nine shots, and the count is deliberate'), and Task 6 Step 3 says 'Desktop web is the v0 target and nine shots is settled'. (3) Global Constraints also says 'Page-level shots only. No `toHaveScreenshot` on a clipped element' - the fix's 'screenshot `.nh-drop-overlay`' is an element shot, and the plan's own determinism study records that the ONLY drift in 60 container runs was 'the anti-aliased rounded corner of an element-CLIPPED shot'. ALSO A CORRECTION TO why_it_matters: 'A regression in the file-drag affordance would ship silently' is only half true. web/e2e/player.e2e.ts already carries THREE passing tests that reach the overlay and assert it - 'dragging a file onto the player opens it' (overlay visible before drop, hidden after), the not-a-score failure path, and 'the drop overlay survives the pointer crossing into a child'. What is unguarded is the overlay's APPEARANCE (dashed outline, blur, scrim), not its presence.
decided_findings.spike: RAN (static; there is no command to execute for an omission, so I measured every premise instead). (a) `grep -ni 'drag' docs/plans/2026-09-29-web-visual-regression-gate.md` returns exactly TWO lines, neither about coverage: the stale-line-number table row for `fileDrag`, and the Task 5 helper comment's `[data-dragging]` aside. So the plan IS silent - confirmed. (b) `grep -rn 'nh-drop-overlay'` over the repo returns four live sites: web/app/globals.css:67, web/app/play/PlayerShell.tsx:1139, the v0a plan, and docs/specs/2026-09-21-web-visual-regression-gate.md:394. `grep -rln 'nh-drop' client/src` returns NOTHING, so 'no client/ Storybook story renders it' is confirmed. (d) web/e2e/player.e2e.ts:334 `fileDrag` does drive CDP `Input.dispatchDragEvent`, so the tooling claim holds. (e) THE SPIKE CORRECTED THE FIX: the same grep found the spec's own deferral paragraph, which the finding does not mention and which already gives this state a recorded reason. So the residual gap is not 'no deferral anywhere' - it is that the plan points at the spec's deferral for the popovers and not for this one.
decided_findings.scenario: You open a chart by dragging the file onto the player. While your finger is still down, the whole window outlines itself in a dashed teal border and the score behind it blurs, so you can see exactly where to let go. Months later someone reworks that outline and it is drawn just outside the edge of the window, where nothing can see it - which has already happened once here. The merge still goes through: none of the nine screenshots ever picks up a file, and the behaviour tests only ask whether the words 'Drop to open' are on screen, never what the surface looks like. Reading this plan you cannot tell whether anyone thought about that, because it says nothing about dragging at all.
decided_findings.whats_wrong: The plan is silent about the drag-over state. Task 4 Step 3's comment block 'TWO THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE ADDING A TENTH SHOT' item 2 points a reader at the spec's recorded deferral for the Settings and Tracks popover shots; the drag-over state has an equally explicit recorded deferral in the same spec (docs/specs/2026-09-21-web-visual-regression-gate.md:394) and gets no such pointer. decided_findings.proposed_fix: Do NOT add a tenth shot. Add a third item to Task 4 Step 3's 'TWO THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE ADDING A TENTH SHOT' comment (retitled THREE) recording the drag-over state, pointing at the deferral the spec already carries, giving the spec's own reason (mid-gesture timing, not missing tooling), and saying plainly what the existing behaviour tests do and do not cover - presence, not appearance. decided_findings.why_it_works: It closes the only real gap - the plan's silence - at the cost of six comment lines, and it does so in the exact idiom the plan already uses one item earlier for the popovers, so the two deferrals read the same way. It does not touch the nine-shot count that three separate places in this document treat as settled, and it does not propose an element-clipped shot, which Global Constraints forbid and the determinism study flags as the one measured source of drift. decided_findings.severity_rationale: P3 holds, and the spike strengthens the case for keeping it there rather than raising it. Nothing breaks either way - the pre-PR checklist runs both compare commands, so a wrong pick surfaces immediately - and the value is purely lower cognitive load at a moment when both values are already being rewritten. What the spike changed is the price, not the band: the finding says 'costs nothing now', and the real cost is a rewritten ordering note plus a ten-occurrence documentation sweep that Task 10 does not currently schedule. That is still small, but it is not nothing, and the human should see it before choosing.
decided_findings.why_it_matters_as_filed: Six months on, pnpm test:vr:docker and pnpm test:web:docker sit next to each other in the same package.json and only one of them says which package it touches; picking the wrong one regenerates the wrong baselines and the web job goes red for a reason the command name gave no hint of. The plan is already rewriting both test:vr:docker* values to call the new helper, so aligning the names costs nothing now and a documentation sweep later. Nothing breaks — the pre-PR checklist runs both compare commands — but this repo's own conventions ask for low cognitive load, and a symmetric pair delivers it for free at this exact moment.
decided_findings.suggested_fix_as_filed: Rename the two client scripts to test:client:docker and test:client:docker:update in Task 3 Step 2 so both pairs name their package, and carry the rename through the client/README.md, runbook and AGENTS.md edits already scheduled in Task 10.
